title: Adjoining a variable cannot decrease conditional mutual information
statement:
Let $X$, $Y$, $W$, and $Z$ be measurable functions on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$, taking values in countable measurable spaces and each having finite range. Then the conditional mutual information satisfies
\[
  I[X : W \mid Z; \mu] \;\le\; I[X : (Y, W) \mid Z; \mu],
\]
where $(Y, W)$ denotes the joint random variable $\omega \mapsto (Y(\omega), W(\omega))$.
hypotheses_covered: values in countable measurable spaces (with measurable singletons)
each of X, Y, W, Z has finite range
replaced:
For measurable $X$, $Y$, $W$, $Z$ with finite ranges under a probability measure,
\[
  I[X : W \mid Z;\mu] \;\le\; I[X : (Y, W) \mid Z;\mu].
\]
